name: New hire identity check + account provisioning with RelayShield

parameters.content:
## New hire identity check + Google Workspace provisioning

**What it does**

When HR adds a new hire, two independent branches run: an identity-risk check on the person's personal email, and Google Workspace account provisioning. Neither blocks the other, so a risky personal email never delays day-one access.

1. Your HR system posts the new hire to the webhook.
2. RelayShield checks that personal email for breach and infostealer exposure.
3. If exposure is found, the result is logged to Notion and Security is alerted in Slack. If clean, only the Notion record is written.
4. In parallel, a Google Workspace account is created from the corporate email.
5. Provisioning success or failure is logged to Notion and IT is notified in Slack.

**Setup**

1. Point your HR system at the webhook URL. The payload needs personal_email, corporate_email, name, department, manager_email, job_title and temp_password.
2. Add RelayShield credentials to both check nodes.
3. Add a Google Workspace Admin OAuth2 credential (see the red note).
4. Add Notion credentials and set the variable notionOnboardingDbId to your audit-log database.
5. Add Slack credentials and set slackSecurityChannelId to your security channel.

**Customization**

Using Microsoft 365? Swap the Google Workspace node for Microsoft Entra ID; the logging and alerting downstream are unchanged. Add more RelayShield checks, such as NHI exposure or identity graph, to broaden the signals.

### 1. Trigger and identity risk checks
The HR webhook starts the run, then RelayShield checks the new hire's  
personal email for breach and infostealer exposure. The IF node  
routes on whether any exposure was found.

### 2. Identity result logging
Every check is written to Notion, so there is an audit trail either way. Security is alerted in Slack only when exposure is actually found.

### 3. Google Workspace provisioning
Runs in parallel with the identity check, so day-one access is never  
blocked. The account is created from the corporate email, then checked  
for success.

**Add your credential:** the Create Google Workspace Account node needs  
a Google Workspace Admin OAuth2 credential that can create users, or  
the workflow will not run.

### 4. Provisioning outcome
Success and failure are both logged to Notion and announced to IT in Slack, so a failed account creation cannot pass silently.

nodes.name: When New Hire Added
nodes.notes: Receives an HTTP POST from your HR system when a new hire is ready to onboard. Expected payload: { "personal_email": "newhire@gmail.com", "corporate_email": "jsmith@company.com", "name": "Jane Smith", "department": "Engineering", "manager_email": "manager@company.com", "job_title": "Software Engineer", "temp_password": "<one-time-password-from-HR-system>" }

nodes.name: Check for Breaches
nodes.notes: Checks the new hire's personal email for known credential breaches — a pre-existing exposure worth security's awareness before this identity gets corporate access, even though it doesn't block day-1 provisioning.

nodes.name: Check for Infostealer Threats
nodes.notes: Checks whether the new hire's personal-email credentials appear in infostealer malware logs — indicating their personal device may already be compromised before they ever touch corporate systems.

nodes.name: If Prior Exposure Detected
nodes.notes: Informational only — does not gate provisioning. Flags a new hire whose personal email already shows breach or infostealer exposure, so security can watch that identity more closely post-onboarding.

nodes.name: Record Exposure in Notion
nodes.notes: Creates a page in your onboarding risk log Notion database, independent of the provisioning outcome below.

parameters.title: ={{ $('When New Hire Added').item.json.name }} — Pre-Existing Exposure Flag

nodes.name: Notify Security in Slack
nodes.notes: Posts an awareness alert to your security/IT Slack channel. Does not block or delay provisioning — that branch runs independently.

textUi.text: ⚠️ New Hire With Pre-Existing Exposure — {{ $('When New Hire Added').item.json.name }}

nodes.name: Record Clean Result in Notion
nodes.notes: Logs a clean result so every onboarding identity check is auditable, even when nothing is found.

parameters.title: ={{ $('When New Hire Added').item.json.name }} — Onboarding Clean (No Prior Exposure)

nodes.name: Create Google Workspace Account
nodes.notes: Fires in parallel with the identity check above, off the same trigger, with zero gap - the new hire gets access on day one regardless of the check's outcome. Using Microsoft 365 instead? Replace this node with a Microsoft Entra ID node - the downstream logging and alerting apply unchanged.

nodes.name: Check Provisioning Success
nodes.notes: Google's Admin SDK returns the created user object (with an `id` field) on success. Logged as its own independent audit event — separate from the identity-check outcome above, same design as the offboarding template's revocation-success tracking.

nodes.name: Record Provisioning Success
nodes.notes: Independent audit trail for provisioning outcome, regardless of what the identity check found.

nodes.name: Notify IT of Account Success
nodes.notes: The onboarding-side notification — confirms the new corporate account actually exists. Mirror of the offboarding template's suspension-confirmation alert, opposite direction.

textUi.text: ✅ *Account provisioned:* {{ $('When New Hire Added').item.json.corporate_email }} is ready — {{ $('When New Hire Added').item.json.name }}, {{ $('When New Hire Added').item.json.job_title }}, {{ $('When New Hire Added').item.json.department }}.

nodes.name: Record Provisioning Failure
nodes.notes: A failed provisioning call needs manual follow-up — logged distinctly from success so it can't get lost in an otherwise-clean audit trail.

nodes.name: Alert IT of Provisioning Issue
nodes.notes: Urgent path — a new hire without working access on day one is a real operational problem, escalated distinctly from a routine success confirmation.

textUi.text: 🚨 Account Provisioning FAILED — {{ $('When New Hire Added').item.json.name }}

Automatic provisioning for {{ $('When New Hire Added').item.json.corporate_email }} did not succeed. This new hire does not have working system access — needs manual account creation before their start date.
